facts.statement: Largirostrornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean bird.
facts.quote: Largirostrornis is a genus of enantiornithean bird.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Largirostrornis is a slab and counterslab found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, China.
facts.quote: Largirostrornis is known from one fossil, slab and counterslab, found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, People's Republic of China.

facts.statement: Largirostrornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the late Aptian age, approximately 120.3 ±0.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Jiufotang Formation is dated to the Early Cretaceous period, late Aptian age, 120.3 ±0.7 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Largirostrornis is cataloged as IVPP 10531 and is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil is in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China. It has been given catalog number IVPP 10531.

facts.statement: In 1997, Largirostrornis was known to have the longest torso of any described Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: L. sexdentornis had in 1997 a torso longer than all other known Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Largirostrornis had a skull approximately 32 millimeters long and was slightly larger than Cuspirostrisornis.
facts.quote: It is slightly larger than Cuspirostrisornis, with a skull about 32 millimeters long.

facts.statement: The paired dentaries and premaxillae of Largirostrornis each contained six teeth.
facts.quote: The paired dentaries and premaxillae each hold six teeth.

facts.statement: Largirostrornis possessed tall neural spines on its cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: There are tall neural spines on the cervical and dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The species Largirostrornis sexdentoris was named and described by Hou Lianhai in 1997.
facts.quote: The species was named and described by Hou Lianhai in 1997.

facts.statement: Some researchers debate whether Largirostrornis sexdentoris is a distinct species or a junior synonym of Cathayornis yandica.
facts.quote: Some researchers believe this species to be a junior synonym of the similar Cathayornis yandica.

facts.statement: The parent group of Largirostrornis is the family Cuspirostrisornithidae.
The time range for Largirostrornis is recorded as the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus name Largirostrornis derives from the Latin words for 'large' and 'beak', while the species name means 'six-toothed'.
rejected.quote: The genus name comes from the Latin words largus, 'large' and rostrum, 'beak', and the specific name means 'six-toothed' from Latin sex and dens.
